title: Persistence of kinks in the NLS equation with competing nonlinearities
authors: P. G. Kevrekidis, D. E. Pelinovsky
abstract: External potentials break the translational invariance of nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equations and generally convert a continuous family of standing wave solutions into isolated pinned states. We study this mechanism for the prototypical case of a kink in the NLS equation with competing focusing cubic and defocusing quintic nonlinearities. The Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction method is used to prove that the location $s_0$ of the pinned kinks is selected near roots of an effective potential $V_{\rm eff}(s)$. We then determine how the translational zero eigenvalue of the Jacobian operator splits under the perturbation and prove that the sign of $V_{\rm eff}'(s_0)$ distinguishes eigendirections of positive and negative energy. We further show that if the Jacobian operator admits a negative eigenvalue, then the stability problem contains a real unstable eigenvalue. The derivation of the asymptotic expansion for the unstable eigenvalue is nonstandard because the zero eigenvalue is embedded in the continuous spectrum of the linearized operator. Finally, we show that the persistence of kinks lacks parity symmetry even if the external potential is odd. Numerical continuation, spectral computations with domains adapted to the slowly decaying eigenfunctions, and direct dynamical simulations of the time evolution corroborate the analytical predictions for different representative examples.
summary: This work analyzes the persistence and stability of kink solutions in a cubic-quintic NLS equation subjected to an external potential. Using advanced mathematical techniques like Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction, the authors establish criteria based on an effective potential to predict if a kink will be stable or unstable. The results confirm that the pinning mechanism is robust and provides detailed insights into the spectral properties of the perturbed system.
main_problem: The paper investigates how kinks (solitary wave solutions) in the Nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation persist when translational invariance is broken by an external potential.
main_result: The persistence of kinks is governed by the roots of an effective potential, and the stability of the pinned state is determined by the sign of the derivative of this effective potential at the root.
method: The analysis employs the Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction method, perturbation theory to analyze eigenvalue splitting, and comparison with numerical continuation and direct dynamical simulations.
model_or_system: The model is the NLS equation with competing focusing cubic and defocusing quintic nonlinearities, perturbed by an external potential V(x). Stationary solutions are sought in the form of kinks.
key_observables: Effective potential V_eff(s), the sign of V'_eff(s_0), and the eigenvalues mu_+ and lambda characterizing the stability.
important_parameters: The small perturbation parameter epsilon (ε) controlling the strength of the external potential V(x).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the validity of the Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction and asymptotic expansions for the eigenvalues, though some long-term stability aspects remain open.
figures_summary: Figure 6 illustrates the dynamical evolution of an unstable kink, showing it emitting radiation and subsequently settling near a stable pinned state.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure moving from the analytical derivation of the pinning mechanism via V_eff, to the spectral stability analysis determining unstable eigenvalues, and concluding with numerical corroboration of these analytical predictions.
why_interesting: The study of nonlinear wave dynamics, particularly the stability and pinning of topological defects like kinks, is highly relevant to nonlinear optics, Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), and nonlinear wave propagation in various physical systems.
